name: Pale Lavender
lede: Pale Lavender is a very light, slightly pink violet, a descriptive name that two color systems list and a few writers use mostly as a mood.

sections.title: A name from lists
sections.body: The library finds Pale Lavender in the xkcd color survey and in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, block 226 [1]. A near-duplicate in the library is Very Light Purple, 2.3 units away, and the closest named color is [[thistle]] at 7.7 units [1]. The name is descriptive: it takes the flower's [[lavender]] and lightens it. Who first used it as a fixed color name is undocumented.

sections.title: Pale lavender in prose
sections.body: Batchelor recalls a television advertisement in which lavender underpants hung on a washing line are stolen, and the story ends in a pale lavender front room [2]. He reads the pair of adverts, this one and a bright yellow sweatshirt, as parables about how words fail to pin down a color [2]. No book in the corpus treats pale lavender as a pigment or dye [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is almost white: lightness 87 of 100, and a contrast of only 1.4 against white [1]. It is also rare in paintings. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has a color within six units of this swatch covering at least five per cent of the canvas [4]. As photographed: museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings; a color match is not a pigment test.
